page: OVHcloud c2-15 is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel processor based on the Haswell microarchitecture without TSX instructions. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores running at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It includes 15.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 100 GB of local SSD storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate a moderate to low processing profile. In single-core stress-ng tests, the instance registers a score of 872.67, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested hardware, while multi-core performance reaches 3481.67, placing it in the bottom 25%. PassMark CPU and memory evaluations show average performance, with a CPU score of 6764.0 and a memory score of 1953.97. Memory bandwidth tests reveal a stark contrast between cached small-block reads at 346.97 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 36.82 GB/sec.

For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates weak performance in cryptographic operations, registering 2252.27 in PassMark encryption tests, and weak results in Redis SET operations at 5.89 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds are average for small 135M models, achieving 476.72 tokens per second for prompt processing, but drop to a poor 11.63 tokens per second for medium 7B models. Given these performance trade-offs, the instance is best suited for light database operations, basic web serving, and general-purpose utility workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores but do not require modern vector or matrix instruction sets.
description: OVHcloud c2-15 is a compute-optimized virtual server instance utilizing the KVM hypervisor and an x86_64 Intel Haswell processor. It is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz, 15.0 GB of RAM, and 100 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark data shows a split performance profile: while cached small-block memory reads perform at an average rate of 346.97 GB/sec, uncached large-block operations and raw CPU compute metrics fall into the lower percentiles, with a stress-ng single-core score of 872.67. The instance lacks advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, limiting its efficiency for modern machine learning workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for legacy applications, basic web serving, and light database operations that require dedicated CPU resources without demanding high-intensity cryptographic or parallel processing capabilities.
